title: Buffers
examples: What is the ratio of the weak acid to its conjugate base in a buffer?
How does the concentration of the buffer components affect the pH?
Can a buffer resist changes in pH when strong acid is added?

explain.say: Today we are learning about buffer solutions in chemistry.
A buffer is typically made from a weak acid and its salt.
The buffer resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.
When acid is added, the conjugate base component reacts with the extra hydrogen ions.
When base is added, the weak acid component reacts with the extra hydroxide ions.
We calculate buffer pH using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.

faq.q: Why is the ratio important for a buffer?
faq.a: The ratio of the conjugate base to the weak acid determines the buffer's strength. If the ratio is 1, the pH is equal to the pKa.
asks: What does the ratio of components control?
How does the concentration ratio affect pH?

faq.q: Can buffers stop all changes in pH?
faq.a: No, buffers can only resist changes in pH up to a certain point. If too much strong acid or base is added, the buffer capacity is exceeded.
asks: Is the pH change completely stopped?
What limits a buffer's ability to resist change?

faq.q: What does pKa represent in the equation?
faq.a: pKa is the negative logarithm of the acid dissociation constant for the weak acid. It is a characteristic value of the acid.
asks: Where do I find the pKa value?
Is pKa related to the strength of the acid?

faq.q: Do I need to calculate the pH every time?
faq.a: You only need to calculate the pH if the ratio of the base to the acid is not one to one. If they are equal, the pH equals the pKa.
asks: What is the easiest pH to calculate?

faq.a: Yes, your blood plasma acts as a buffer system to keep your pH within a very narrow range. This is vital for life processes.
asks: What is the body's main buffer system?

facts: A buffer resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added.
Buffers are mixtures containing a weak acid and its salt (which provides the conjugate base).
The pH of a buffer solution can be calculated using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation.
When the concentration of the weak acid equals the conjugate base, the pH equals the pKa.

quiz.say: A buffer is made from which two components?

options.show: Weak acid and its conjugate base salt
options.say: Weak acid and its conjugate base salt

quiz.why: The salt provides the necessary conjugate base component to neutralize added acid.

wrong.0: A strong base cannot maintain a stable pH when acid is added.
wrong.1: Water alone cannot buffer changes in pH.
wrong.3: The weak acid alone cannot neutralize added base effectively.

quiz.say: If the concentration of the weak acid equals the conjugate base, what is the pH?

options.show: The pH equals the pKa value
options.say: The pH equals the pKa value

quiz.why: When the ratio is one to one, the log term becomes zero, leaving only the pKa.
